class_create_owner.A: The sample is Greg KH's tree-wide commit 1aaba11da9aa ("driver core: class: remove module * from class_create()", 2023-03-17), which changes every caller in one go. The old regex (class_create(THIS_MODULE,) is precise. The new regex (class_create( not followed by THIS_MODULE) can also match calls that are not part of this change, such as class_create(owner, ...) wrappers or the old __class_create. Only one row was sampled, so the class_create( matches added outside this commit have not been checked.
class_create_owner.B: There was only one sample, from Greg KH's tree-wide commit 1aaba11da9aa ("driver core: class: remove module * from class_create()"). That commit changed the class_create() signature and updated callers in the same change, so it is a pure mechanical API migration. The old regex (class_create(THIS_MODULE,) is specific, and the new regex (class_create( with a first argument other than THIS_MODULE) matches the post-change calls cleanly. One possible source of noise: the new regex can also match callers added after the API change, such as new drivers, which would not be migrations.

dev_err_probe.A: The old regex '\bdev_err\s*\(' matches every dev_err call, but dev_err is not deprecated; only probe-path error reporting (dev_err followed by returning the error) is a dev_err_probe candidate. So old_left_after_commit (raw git grep -c) overstates what is left: most hits are runtime or non-probe messages. I judged 'partial' only when dev_err-and-return-error paths remained in the same probe function (or the probe helper the commit touched). All 8 samples are real conversions; none are coincidental. Commits are usually targeted, converting one to a few call sites, so 'partial' is common under this definition. Also, dev_err_probe is not a 1:1 rename: it takes an extra error argument and returns it, so it usually collapses 'dev_err(...); return err;' into 'return dev_err_probe(dev, err, ...)'. #3 also changed the condition from 'status < 0' to 'if (status)', which looks semantically wrong, but that does not affect whether it is a migration.
dev_err_probe.B: The old regex \bdev_err\s*\( matches every dev_err call. dev_err is not deprecated: dev_err_probe only fits probe-time error paths that return an error code. So the raw old_left counts overstate how incomplete each commit is; runtime, IRQ, transfer and suspend paths legitimately keep dev_err. Verdicts here count a commit as partial only when dev_err calls on error-return paths remain in the probe function or probe-only helpers. These commits are usually targeted (one or a few call sites, often to silence an -EPROBE_DEFER message), so most are partial under a strict reading. Sample #3 also adds a regression: 'if (status)' after platform_get_irq treats a valid IRQ as an error. Sample #2's main purpose is unrelated (dropping a platform_data check), and the dev_err_probe change is a 'while at it' side change.
dev_err_probe.T: The old regex \bdev_err\s*\( matches every dev_err call, including runtime and diagnostic prints that could never become dev_err_probe, so old_left_after_commit overstates how much conversion remains. Commits like this one deliberately convert only the probe() function. Whether such a commit counts as genuine or partial depends on probe-path helper functions that return deferrable errors. Here, svs_bank_resource_setup and svs_get_efuse_data still use plain dev_err on those paths.

device_get_match_data.B: All 8 samples are genuine: the old and new regexes are close and specific (of_device_get_match_data( versus device_get_match_data(), and the \b boundary keeps the new regex from matching the old call. All 8 commits remove one of_device_get_match_data call and add the matching device_get_match_data call on the same line, and the completeness grep finds 0 old calls left in every file. Several of these are larger fwnode/device-property conversions (ds1307, at91-sama5d2, tegra186 ACPI support) or refactors (mtk-cmdq pdata), where the API swap comes along with other changes. In sample #4, the swap appears late in a long diff (around line 239), beyond what a quick look at the first part of the diff shows. One thing to watch: header churn (of_device.h removed or added) happens alongside the swap and is not itself a sign that old usage remains.
device_get_match_data.A: The OLD regex \bof_device_get_match_data\s*\( cannot match device_get_match_data( on its own, because the "of_" prefix and \b keep them apart, and the NEW regex \bdevice_get_match_data cannot match inside of_device_get_match_data, because the underscore breaks the word boundary. So the regexes separate the two APIs cleanly. All 8 samples are one-for-one call replacements, usually with an include change (of_device.h/of.h -> property.h/mod_devicetable.h), and none leave an old call in the file. In one sample (#4, mtk-cmdq-mailbox) the swap is incidental to a larger refactor but still deliberate. Most samples come from Andy Shevchenko-style "make use of device properties" series or Rob Herring's tree-wide conversion (#6).

devm_clk_get_enabled.A: The OLD regex matches only clk_prepare_enable(), but the real migration replaces the pair devm_clk_get[_optional] + clk_prepare_enable (+ clk_disable_unprepare in error and remove paths) with devm_clk_get[_optional]_enabled. The leftover counts therefore pick up clk_prepare_enable calls in suspend/resume, runtime-PM or clock-gating paths, and on clocks the driver registers itself. Those cannot be converted, so a nonzero count is not a reliable partial signal for this migration. Every sampled leftover was one of these, so none was judged partial. Sample #0 is an unusual case: a driver-local duplicate helper (devm_clk_get_enable) is removed in favour of the new core API. Several commits come from series that convert many drivers (Huawei authors, 2023) and usually carry the Fixes/cleanup wording.
devm_clk_get_enabled.B: The OLD regex (\bclk_prepare_enable\s*\() is much broader than the migration: devm_clk_get_enabled only replaces the probe-time pattern of devm_clk_get + clk_prepare_enable (+ the matching disable on error and remove paths). Leftover clk_prepare_enable hits are mostly in runtime PM, resume or clock-gating functions, or on clocks that were not obtained with devm_clk_get (for example devm_clk_register). Those uses cannot be converted, so a nonzero old_left_after_commit overstates incompleteness here, and all such leftovers in this sample were of that kind. Several commits are framed as error-path fixes (Fixes: tags) but carry out the conversion all the same. Sample #0 replaces a driver-local duplicate helper devm_clk_get_enable() with the core API.

devm_platform_ioremap.A: Samples 0-6 are textbook conversions: platform_get_resource[_byname] plus devm_ioremap_resource(dev, res) become devm_platform_[get_and_]ioremap_resource[_byname](pdev, ...). Each file has 0 OLD matches left after the commit. One source of noise: the OLD regex also matches comments that mention devm_ioremap_resource(. In sample 7 the only deleted OLD hit is a comment. The NEW helper there replaces devm_ioremap(), not devm_ioremap_resource(), inside a refactor into per-version ops. A pair of OLD and NEW hits on the same commit therefore does not prove a conversion unless the deleted OLD line is code.
devm_platform_ioremap.B: The old regex \bdevm_ioremap_resource\s*\( also matches comment text such as "devm_ioremap_resource()." (sample #7), which gives false positives. Typical genuine commits replace a platform_get_resource[_byname]() + devm_ioremap_resource() pair with devm_platform_[get_and_]ioremap_resource[_byname](). Some commits instead move from devm_ioremap() (no request_mem_region) to the platform helper. That is a different, semantics-changing conversion, and the old regex does not cover it. Samples #0 to #6 are single-file cleanups (Huawei/Alibaba/vivo/Linaro series), and each leaves 0 old usages.

dma_set_mask_and_coherent.A: All 8 samples are genuine and complete: no dma_set_coherent_mask( calls are left in any of the files after the commit. The old regex only catches dma_set_coherent_mask(. The paired dma_set_mask( calls that are removed alongside it are a real part of the migration, but the regex does not match them. Most commits are from the 2021-2022 cleanup series (Takashi Iwai's sound patches and Christophe Jaillet's 'Use dma_set_mask_and_coherent() and simplify code' series), which also removes the 64-to-32-bit fallback as dead code. In sample #0 the subject is an unrelated error-code fix, but the commit still performs the migration.
dma_set_mask_and_coherent.B: All 8 samples are genuine and fully converted: each file had 0 dma_set_coherent_mask( matches right after the commit. The migration is a consolidation, not a 1:1 rename. A dma_set_mask()+dma_set_coherent_mask() pair, often inside a 64-bit-then-32-bit fallback, collapses into one dma_set_mask_and_coherent(). Many of these commits (Christophe JAILLET's 2022 series) also drop the 32-bit fallback and the HIGHDMA flag logic as dead code. So the diffs are larger than the API swap and include behaviour-neutral refactors. The old regex only catches dma_set_coherent_mask and misses the paired dma_set_mask calls being removed. Sample #0's subject ('fix error return code') hides the migration, so subject-based filtering would miss it. One adjacent row in the CSV, pci_dma_wrappers#0 (emu10k1x, 'Use dma_set_mask_and_coherent to simplify code'), sits under a different migration id but matches this API, which suggests overlap between the two migration definitions.

eth_hw_addr_set.A: All 8 samples are genuine and complete, with 0 old-API matches left after each commit. They come from the 2021 series that made netdev->dev_addr const; the commits landed in Oct-Nov 2021 under one author's subjects such as "use eth_hw_addr_set()". The old regex catches memcpy() and ether_addr_copy() into *->dev_addr, and the hits are precise here. The new regex also accepts dev_addr_set(), the non-Ethernet member of the same API family (skfddi uses it). Writes the regex does not cover, such as per-byte dev->dev_addr[i] = x, or memcpy into dev_addr + offset, would be missed. One commit (#7, tsnep) also swaps one call for dev_set_mac_address(), which is a different API, alongside the eth_hw_addr_set() change.
eth_hw_addr_set.B: All 8 samples come from the Oct-Nov 2021 tree-wide effort by Jakub Kicinski to make netdev->dev_addr const. Each one replaces memcpy/ether_addr_copy(dev->dev_addr, ...) with eth_hw_addr_set() (or dev_addr_set() for non-Ethernet addresses such as FDDI), and every file has 0 old-regex matches right after the commit. The old regex only catches memcpy/ether_addr_copy. It misses other direct writes to dev_addr, such as driver-specific copy helpers, dev_addr[i] = x assignments or reading the address straight into dev_addr (e.g. atmel.c), so a file can still be incomplete while showing 0 matches. Generic dev->dev_addr reads (memcpy(&hdr.addr2, dev->dev_addr, ...)) do not match the old regex because dev_addr must be the first argument, which keeps false positives low.

fallthrough.A: All 8 samples are clean 1:1 swaps of the '/* fall through */' comment for the 'fallthrough;' pseudo-keyword (Gustavo Silva's tree-wide Clang -Wimplicit-fallthrough effort, 2020-2021, split into one commit per driver). The old regex matches only the comment form, and the new regex matches only the keyword statement, so on this migration the regexes are very precise. The one variation is #2 (si_dpm.c): the annotation also moves from below an #endif to above it, which was the actual Clang fix. In every sample, git grep found 0 old-style comments left in the file after the commit.
fallthrough.B: All 8 samples are single-file Clang fall-through fixes. Each one does a direct 1:1 swap of a '/* fall through */' comment for the 'fallthrough;' pseudo-keyword, with no other changes. The old regex matched 0 lines in every file after its commit. A wider case-insensitive search for any '/*' or '//' fall-through comment also found nothing, so every conversion is complete. The regex pair is very precise for this migration because the old line is removed and the new line added in the same hunk. The one oddity is si_dpm.c (#2), where the keyword was placed inside the #ifdef block.

gpiod_from_of_gpio.A: All 8 samples are clean conversions from the legacy integer GPIO API to GPIO descriptors, usually titled 'switch to using gpiod API' or 'Convert to GPIO descriptors' (many are Dmitry Torokhov's tree-wide of_gpio removal series). Each commit also drops the #include <linux/of_gpio.h> line, and none leaves an old-API match in the file. The 'old' regex reliably finds of_get_named_gpio(_flags) removals. The 'new' regex also matches devm_fwnode_gpiod_get (sample #5) through the optional fwnode_ prefix. Because \\bgpiod_get also matches gpiod_get_value( (the \\s*\\( needs the paren right after 'get', so gpiod_get_value does not actually match), the new regex is precise here. One caveat: some conversions replace a getter with jack descriptor plumbing (gpiod_dev) rather than a gpiod_get call, as #6 does for hp-det.
gpiod_from_of_gpio.B: All 8 samples are dedicated "convert to GPIO descriptors / switch to gpiod API" commits. Each one removes the of_get_named_gpio{,_flags} lookup together with its devm_gpio_request{,_one} call and adds a devm_[fwnode_]gpiod_get[_optional] call for the same property, usually with the "-gpios" suffix dropped from the con_id. Most also replace the linux/of_gpio.h include with linux/gpio/consumer.h. After the commit, git grep finds 0 old-API matches in every file, so there are no partial conversions. The old regex is precise. The new regex correctly covers the devm_fwnode_gpiod_get variant (#5). One caveat: in a few drivers a lookup can move to a framework helper instead of a gpiod_get call (in #6 the hp-det GPIO goes through the jack gpiod_dev), so the counts of matching -old and +new lines may not pair one-to-one.

i2c_probe_new.A: All 8 samples belong to the 2023 tree-wide series (Uwe Kleine-König) that moves i2c_driver initializers from .probe_new back to .probe, once .probe had taken the single-argument signature. Each per-file diff is a one-line rename of the initializer, so the old/new regexes match exactly and add no noise. The completeness grep returned no output for every file, meaning 0 old matches remain. One caveat on the new regex '\.probe\s*=': in general it also matches .probe initializers of other driver types (platform, spi, and so on). So outside this sample, commits that add new non-i2c drivers could show up as false positives. The old regex '\.probe_new\s*=' is specific to i2c (and a few related buses).
i2c_probe_new.B: All 8 samples are genuine and complete. Each is a one-line swap of .probe_new for .probe inside a struct i2c_driver initializer, written by one author (Uwe Kleine-König) as part of the 2023 tree-wide series. In that series the i2c core first changed .probe to take one argument (v6.3) and the drivers then switched back from .probe_new. In every file the diff changes only that one line, and git grep counts 0 .probe_new matches after the commit. Caveat: the 'new' regex '\.probe\s*=' is very broad. It also matches .probe for platform, spi, usb and other drivers, so outside this tree-wide series it would produce false positives unless the hit is limited to i2c_driver structs or paired with a removed .probe_new line in the same hunk.

i2c_remove_void.A: The old regex matches any static int function that takes a struct i2c_client* as its only argument. That includes probe_new callbacks and internal helpers such as *_gpio_uninit and *_chip_exit, so git grep -c counts are inflated: after a genuine conversion the remaining hit is usually the probe function, not a leftover remove callback. False positives come from two sources. First, helper functions changed from int to void for error-handling reasons before the 2022 API change. Second, pure renames where the remove callback still returns int. The real migration is the tree-wide commit ed5c2f5fd10d ('i2c: Make remove callback return void', 2022-08-15) plus follow-up fixups for drivers that were added later or missed. Some of those fixups change only a forward declaration. A more precise check would require the function name to end in _remove, or would cross-check the .remove = assignment.
i2c_remove_void.B: The OLD/NEW regexes match any static function that takes a single struct i2c_client* argument, not just the .remove callback. So every file's completeness count includes the probe function (which correctly stays int) and often helper functions such as *_init. A count above 0 does not mean the conversion is incomplete; you have to check whether the remaining hit is the remove callback itself. False positives come from three sources: helper functions whose return type changed to void (e.g. *_gpio_uninit, *_chip_exit), preparatory 2021-2022 cleanups that make remove return 0, and renames where a static void shutdown(struct i2c_client*) matches the NEW pattern. The genuine set is the tree-wide core commit ed5c2f5fd10d plus later fixups for drivers that commit missed, either late-added drivers or forward declarations.

ida_simple.A: All 8 samples are genuine and complete: in every file, 0 old-API matches remain after the commit. The old regex (ida_simple_get/ida_simple_remove followed by '(') is precise and gave no false positives in this sample. The new regex matches the replacement variants as expected: ida_alloc, ida_alloc_max, ida_alloc_range and ida_free. The conversions are mostly mechanical. Exclusive upper bounds become inclusive ones, e.g. 'max - 1' for ida_alloc_max, and (0, 0) bounds become plain ida_alloc. One sample (nouveau #1) is titled as a leak fix, but it does the fix by converting to ida_alloc_max(..., 99, ...), so it still counts as a migration. Many commits come from a tree-wide series by one author with subjects like 'Remove usage of the deprecated ida_simple_xx() API' or 'Directly use ida_alloc()/free()'.
ida_simple.B: All 8 samples are clean in-place 1:1 conversions: ida_simple_get(ida,0,0,gfp) -> ida_alloc, ida_simple_get(ida,0,max,gfp) -> ida_alloc_max(max-1), ida_simple_get(ida,min,max,...) -> ida_alloc_range, and ida_simple_remove -> ida_free. The old regex finds 0 matches in every file after its commit. The old/new regexes are precise for this migration and no coincidental hits were found. Commit subjects are mostly the explicit 'Remove usage of the deprecated ida_simple_xx() API' / 'Directly use ida_alloc()/free()' series (2022-2024). One sample (nouveau) is mainly a leak fix that does the conversion as well, and it still counts as genuine. The ida_alloc_max conversions move the exclusive end to an inclusive max (the '- 1'), which is a semantic detail to keep in mind for benchmark ground truth.

in_hardirq.A: All three samples come from the 2021 tree-wide series that replaced the deprecated in_irq() with in_hardirq(). Each commit is a pure mechanical rename with the same meaning. The old regex \bin_irq\s*\(\s*\) also matches comments: dm-crypt had one comment hit, which the commit also updated. Watch for comment-only hits in other files. The regex does not catch in_irq without parentheses, as in macro references, but there were none here.
in_hardirq.B: All three samples come from Changbin Du's tree-wide series from August 2021, which replaces the deprecated in_irq() macro with in_hardirq(). Each one is a pure one-to-one mechanical rename that leaves the file with no in_irq() calls. The regexes are precise for this migration because in_irq()/in_hardirq() are argument-less macros with distinctive names. One source of noise: the old regex also matches comments that mention in_irq() (dm-crypt has one, which this commit updated), so a raw count could include comment hits.

irq_affinity_hint.A: All 8 samples are genuine and complete: after each commit the file has 0 matches for the old regex. Six of them come from Thomas Gleixner's / Nitesh Lal's tree-wide series of 2021-12-10, which deprecated irq_set_affinity_hint(). Each driver had its own commit, and the series used two targets: irq_update_affinity_hint() where only the hint should be set, and irq_set_affinity_and_hint() where the driver really wants the affinity applied. The later commits from 2022 and 2024 follow the same pattern. The regexes are precise for this migration because the old and new names are distinct function names with no prefix overlap; the only extra hits are comment lines, which change along with the calls. Note that calls passing NULL sometimes go to irq_set_affinity_and_hint() (qcom-cpufreq-hw) and sometimes to irq_update_affinity_hint(). Both count as the new API.
irq_affinity_hint.B: The commits from 2021-12-10 are one tree-wide series that deprecated irq_set_affinity_hint(). In it, NULL/hint-only calls became irq_update_affinity_hint() and calls that also need to set affinity became irq_set_affinity_and_hint(). The 2022 and 2024 commits are later cleanups of the same deprecated call. The old regex '\birq_set_affinity_hint\s*\(' is precise. In these samples it hit no comments or lookalike APIs: comment hits such as 'hint for irq_set_affinity_hint.' have no '(' and did not match. The old-call count after the commit was 0 for every file. Note that irq_set_affinity_and_hint(irq, NULL) is a valid like-for-like replacement for the old irq_set_affinity_hint(irq, NULL), so either new API counts as a correct target.

kmap_local.A: All 8 sampled commits are clean, file-scoped kmap_atomic()->kmap_local_page() conversions with matching kunmap_atomic()->kunmap_local() changes. Most come from the 2022-2023 highmem deprecation campaign (Fabio De Francesco, Ira Weiny, Zhao Liu, Adrian Hunter). After each commit the file has 0 matches for the old regex '\bkmap_atomic\s*\(' (git grep exited 1 with no output every time), so none is partial. The old regex skips kunmap_atomic because of the \b word boundary, which is the right behaviour. One sample (#0) also converts plain kmap()/kunmap() as part of the same change. No regex noise showed up in this sample.
kmap_local.B: I checked all 8 sampled files. Each is a dedicated kmap_atomic -> kmap_local_page conversion whose subject names the migration, with the matching kunmap_atomic -> kunmap_local swaps. The count of OLD-regex matches in the file after each commit is 0. I found no coincidental hits and no incomplete conversions. Several are from the 2022-2023 tree-wide kmap_atomic deprecation series: the Fabio M. De Francesco / Ira Weiny style sfc and mmc conversions, and Zhao Liu's three-commit i915 series dated 2023-12-15. Some commits also tidy nearby code (atomisp merges a kmap() branch; i915 renames variables and adds offset_in_page arithmetic). The OLD regex \bkmap_atomic\s*\( does not match kmap_atomic_prot or kmap_atomic_pfn variants, so a nonzero remaining count from those variants would be missed. That did not matter for these samples.

kobj_default_groups.A: All 8 samples are part of the late-2021/early-2022 tree-wide series replacing the deprecated kobj_type.default_attrs with default_groups (mostly by Greg KH, subject "use default_groups in kobj_type"), typically adding ATTRIBUTE_GROUPS(x) and switching .default_attrs = x_attrs to .default_groups = x_groups. The single-line regexes match this cleanly and there were no false positives. md.c (sample #0, from Christoph Hellwig's md series) converted only md_ktype and left rdev_ktype on default_attrs, so it is partial.
kobj_default_groups.B: All 8 samples come from the 2021-12 to 2022-01 tree-wide series (mostly by Greg KH, plus hch's md patch) that moved struct kobj_type from .default_attrs to .default_groups ahead of removing default_attrs. The regexes are precise for this migration: each hit is a matched -.default_attrs / +.default_groups pair in a kobj_type, usually alongside a new ATTRIBUTE_GROUPS(x) line. The only partial case is md.c, where hch converted only md_ktype and left rdev_ktype for a later commit. Read-only git commands in the container printed 'Auto packing the repository in background' messages, which means git auto-gc fires even on reads; setting gc.auto=0 or passing -c gc.auto=0 would avoid repository writes during verification.

kstrto.A: All three sampled commits are deliberate conversions from simple_strto* to kstrto* (the KSPP deprecation work). Two are complete. ipw2200.c is partial: two simple_strtol() calls are still in the file. The new API can have a different name from the old one (simple_strtol -> kstrtoint), so a migration may not be a one-for-one rename. These conversions also often rewrite the nearby parsing and error-handling code, because kstrto* returns an error code instead of an end pointer. The old regex counted only real code calls in these files, with no matches from comments.
kstrto.B: The old regex (simple_strto{ul,l,ull,ll}) and new regex (kstrto*) match these commits cleanly. All three subjects say outright that they convert simple_strto* to kstrto*. The new call often uses a different width or signedness (for example simple_strtol becomes kstrtoint), and the conversion usually also removes hand-written parsing (prefix stripping, a memcpy into a buffer, end-pointer checks), so the diffs are bigger than a plain rename. A single function can hold several call sites, so counting what remains in the file is what tells genuine from partial. Here ipw2200.c still has 2 simple_strtol calls after the commit.

napi_weight.A: The migration has two steps. In spring 2022, drivers with a non-default weight moved to netif_napi_add_weight() (e.g. 8ded532c, caf6b7f8). Then b48b89f9 (Sep 2022) dropped the weight argument from netif_napi_add() across the tree, in one large tree-wide commit. The 'new' regex '\bnetif_napi_add(?:_weight)?\s*\(' also matches old-style calls, so any commit that moves or re-indents an old 4-argument call shows up as a false positive (veth refactors, the r8152 new-chips commit). There is also an April 2022 series that only replaces driver-private weight defines with NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT (bgmac, smsc9420). It touches the right lines but leaves the old 4-argument API in place, so I classed it as not_migration. Real migrations either add '_weight' or drop the 4th argument. A reliable filter: a '+' line that matches the old regex means the commit is not a migration.
napi_weight.B: The old regex catches any 4-argument netif_napi_add with a weight, and the new regex also matches plain netif_napi_add(. So any moved, re-indented or re-valued netif_napi_add line hits both regexes. These include the veth code moves (#0, #2), the r8152 new-chip rework (#1) and the 2022-04 commits that only replace driver-local weight defines (BGMAC_WEIGHT, NAPI_WEIGHT) with NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT (#3, #4). Those are false positives. The real migration came in two steps. In May 2022 drivers with custom weights moved to netif_napi_add_weight (#5, #6). In Sept 2022 commit b48b89f9c189 dropped the weight argument tree-wide, so NAPI_POLL_WEIGHT callers became 3-argument netif_napi_add (#7). A tighter "new" regex would require netif_napi_add_weight, or a netif_napi_add call with exactly 3 arguments.

netif_rx_ni.A: All samples come from Sebastian Andrzej Siewior's March 2022 tree-wide series of per-subsystem "Use netif_rx()" commits. They followed the change that made netif_rx() callable from any context, which made netif_rx_ni() redundant. The commits are clean 1:1 renames. The one exception is brcmfmac, which also removes the inirq flag that had picked between netif_rx and netif_rx_ni. The old/new regexes are precise for this migration. The only noise risk is \bnetif_rx\s*\( matching unrelated added lines, and the \b keeps wrappers like brcmf_netif_rx( from matching. No partial conversions were found in the sample.
netif_rx_ni.B: All 8 samples come from Sebastian Andrzej Siewior's March 2022 series that removed netif_rx_ni(). Once netif_rx() could be called from any context, every netif_rx_ni(x) caller was mechanically switched to netif_rx(x). The old regex \bnetif_rx_ni\s*\( is precise. The word boundary means the new regex \bnetif_rx\s*\( won't match netif_rx_ni or brcmf_netif_rx. It can still hit unrelated existing netif_rx() calls in moved or added code, but nothing like that came up here. The only non-trivial case is brcmfmac (#4): there the context-dependent if/else (inirq) dispatch was collapsed and the inirq parameter was removed. Every file had 0 old usages left after its commit.

of_property_present.A: All 8 samples come from Rob Herring's 2023 tree-wide series "Use of_property_present() for testing DT property presence" (plus one later ASoC follow-up), so every one is a real one-line conversion. The old regex is too broad for completeness checks. It matches of_property_read_bool() on genuinely boolean properties, which is correct usage and does not need converting. It also matches of_find_property() calls that fetch the struct property pointer (prop = of_find_property(...)), which are not presence tests. A count above 0 after the commit therefore does not by itself mean the conversion is incomplete. Only remaining presence tests of the form if (of_find_property(np, "x", NULL)), or of_property_read_bool on a non-bool property, should count as leftovers. In drivers/of/property.c (#0), the gpio-hog check and the fwnode property_present callback are real leftovers, so #0 is partial. The hits left in #1 and #2 are boolean reads, so those stay genuine.
of_property_present.B: The old regex (of_find_property / of_property_read_bool) is broad. of_find_property is still correct when the caller uses the returned struct property*. of_property_read_bool is correct for real boolean DT properties. Only presence-check calls (of_find_property(..., NULL) used as a truth value, or read_bool on non-boolean properties) are the migration target. So a nonzero completeness count often counts legitimate leftovers: each remaining hit has to be checked by hand, as was done for #0, #1 and #2. All 8 sampled commits are from the 2023 series by Rob Herring and others ("Use of_property_present() for testing DT property presence"); each changes one or two lines mechanically. One process note: a read-only git log run in the container started git's automatic background repacking ("Auto packing the repository in background"). I did not run gc myself, and I stopped the slow command.

pci_alloc_irq_vectors.A: Four samples were checked, and all four are clean, complete conversions. Every commit also replaces the matching teardown call (pci_disable_msi/pci_disable_msix) with pci_free_irq_vectors, and three replace msix_entry[].vector lookups with pci_irq_vector(); the old regex does not track either of these. The old regex covers pci_enable_msi(), pci_enable_msix(), pci_enable_msix_range() and pci_enable_msix_exact(), which together are the right set of deprecated calls. Because it is anchored on "pci_enable_msi", it should not match unrelated identifiers like pci_enable_device. Sample #0 is a lifetime and devm cleanup whose title does not mention the API, but the API swap is real. So judging these commits by their subject lines alone would undercount genuine migrations.
pci_alloc_irq_vectors.B: I looked for reasons to reject each sample, but all four are genuine conversions to pci_alloc_irq_vectors. In each one, a removed pci_enable_msi* line and an added pci_alloc_irq_vectors line belong to the same allocation, and no old API is left in the file (0 matches for all four). Each conversion follows the same pattern: the old call goes, the driver stops keeping its own msix_entry table and uses pci_irq_vector() for IRQ numbers, and pci_disable_msi(x) becomes pci_free_irq_vectors. The old regex only matches the enable calls, not pci_disable_msi(x), so the completeness check only looks at the enable side. Sample #0's commit message is about devm lifetime rather than API deprecation, but the diff still does a direct API swap. Sample #3 converts the plain MSI call (pci_enable_msi) rather than MSI-X, which the regex's optional 'x' covers.

pci_dma_constants.A: All 8 samples come from the Christophe JAILLET / Cai Huoqing series of pci_ to dma_ API switches (2020-2022), which retired include/linux/pci-dma-compat.h. The old and new regexes match whole-word constant names, and the PCI_DMA_* to DMA_* rename here is a pure 1:1 mechanical rename, so the regexes hit cleanly with no coincidental matches. Each converted file had zero PCI_DMA_* constants left after its commit. Matching diff lines are often bare argument-continuation lines (e.g. "PCI_DMA_FROMDEVICE);") because the change happens alongside the pci_map_*/pci_unmap_* to dma_map_*/dma_unmap_* call conversion.
pci_dma_constants.B: All 8 samples come from Christophe JAILLET's series replacing 'pci_' with 'dma_' (2020-2022), plus the final removal of pci-dma-compat.h. In each one the PCI_DMA_* constants are replaced one-for-one with DMA_* in the same expressions, and the file has 0 PCI_DMA_* left after the commit. The regex is precise for this migration: PCI_DMA_* names have no other meaning, so the matches are not coincidental. A single-line diff matcher can be confused because many pairs are rewrapped across lines, with the old constant on a continuation line and the new one joined to other arguments. The conversions often come together with pci_map_* -> dma_map_* call changes in the same commit.

pci_dma_wrappers.A: This migration is the pci-dma-compat.h wrapper removal, done mostly by Christophe JAILLET with coccinelle in 2020-2022. Most sample commits are clean, file-complete conversions that also change PCI_DMA_* to DMA_* constants. The OLD regex does not exclude comments, so commits that only fix comments (e.g. #5, skfddi 'Fix a function name in comments') produce false positives. Variants of pci_set_dma_mask with pci_set_consistent_dma_mask often collapse into a single dma_set_mask_and_coherent, so a 2:1 old:new line ratio is normal. After the commit, the old-API grep returned 0 matches for every sample.
pci_dma_wrappers.B: All seven genuine samples come from the kernel-janitors effort (Christophe JAILLET and others, 2020-2022) to remove the include/linux/pci-dma-compat.h wrappers. Each is a mechanical pci_X -> dma_X conversion with &pdev->dev as the first argument, and alloc gains a GFP flag. The main noise pattern is changes to comments only (#5: 'Fix a function name in comments'). Here a comment mentioning pci_map_single is updated to dma_map_single, so both regexes match but no code changes. The regexes should exclude lines that start with comment markers (' *', '//'). Another blind spot: much of these commits only renames the PCI_DMA_* direction constants (PCI_DMA_TODEVICE -> DMA_TO_DEVICE), and neither regex covers that. In #3 (bnx2) the function calls had mostly been converted earlier, and the only regex hits are the mask calls. None of the sampled files has old-API usage left after its commit.

platform_remove_new.A: All 8 samples are Uwe Kleine-Koenig's tree-wide 'Convert to platform remove callback returning void' series. Each one changes 'static int X_remove' to 'static void X_remove', drops 'return 0;', and swaps '.remove =' for '.remove_new ='. The old regex '\.remove\s*=\s*\w+' matches the .remove field of any driver struct, so it also hits non-platform drivers such as serdev, i2c, spi or mdio. Treat an old_left_after_commit count above 0 with care: in hci_bcm.c the leftover hit is a serdev_device_driver, not a platform_driver. Also note this migration was later reversed: once all drivers were converted, .remove_new was renamed back to .remove (now returning void). Commits from late 2024 onward that turn '.remove_new' into '.remove' therefore match the OLD regex on '+' lines, and the pair can look like a migration in the opposite direction.
platform_remove_new.B: All 8 samples come from Uwe Kleine-Koenig's tree-wide series "Convert to platform remove callback returning void" (2023-2024). Each one changes the callback from int to void, drops `return 0;`, and switches `.remove =` to `.remove_new =` in the platform_driver. The OLD regex `\.remove\s*=\s*\w+` is broad: it also matches `.remove` in other bus driver structs (serdev, i2c_driver, spi_driver and so on). So a nonzero remaining count can be a false "partial", as in hci_bcm.c, where the leftover hit is a serdev_device_driver. Remaining counts should be checked against the struct type. Note also that later in the kernel's history (around v6.11-6.13) `.remove_new` was renamed back to `.remove` with a void return. A regex reversal would therefore flag that later rename as the old API, even though the new-style signature is being kept.

pm_ops_macros.A: All 8 samples are genuine and complete: git grep finds 0 old-macro matches in each file after its commit. The old regex is specific because the SET_ prefix, SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS( and UNIVERSAL_DEV_PM_OPS( are distinctive. Because of the \b word boundary, the old pattern does not match the new DEFINE_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS( or EXPORT_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS(, and the new SYSTEM_SLEEP_PM_OPS( pattern does not match inside SET_SYSTEM_SLEEP_PM_OPS(. Conversions take several forms: DEFINE_SIMPLE/RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS, SET_* changed to the bare *_PM_OPS macros, open-coded fields wrapped in pm_ptr/pm_sleep_ptr (hda_codec), and per-file ops moved into an EXPORT_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS in another file (adxl34x). Some commits mix the migration with feature work (btmtksdio adds system-suspend wakeup support while replacing UNIVERSAL_DEV_PM_OPS). The pm_ptr( part of the new regex can also match code that did not change macros, since pm_ptr existed before this migration, so pm_ptr-only hits need a manual check.
pm_ops_macros.B: All 8 samples are genuine conversions, and none leaves an old-macro use in its file afterwards (every git grep -c exited 1 with no output). Most are Jonathan Cameron / Paul Cercueil style mechanical conversions: SIMPLE/UNIVERSAL_DEV_PM_OPS -> DEFINE_SIMPLE/RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS plus pm_ptr/pm_sleep_ptr, with __maybe_unused dropped. Three samples don't follow that pattern. #5 (adxl34x-i2c.c) moves the definition into a shared file using EXPORT_GPL_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS, so this file only gets pm_sleep_ptr; the new regex catches this only through pm_sleep_ptr, and hdr_new would miss the EXPORT_* variants. #6 (btmtksdio) is a feature commit that happens to replace UNIVERSAL_DEV_PM_OPS. #7 (hda_codec) replaces SET_RUNTIME_PM_OPS with explicit pm_ptr()/pm_sleep_ptr() field assignments rather than RUNTIME_PM_OPS(). Watch-out: in principle the pm_ptr( alternative in the new regex could match unrelated .pm = pm_ptr(&x) edits, but no such false positive appeared in this sample.

spi_get_chipselect.A: The old regex '->chip_select\b' is too broad. In drivers/spi/spi.c it also matches spi_board_info 'chip->chip_select', ACPI 'lookup->chip_select' and comments such as 'spi->chip_select[0]', none of which are spi_device accesses. So a nonzero count left in spi.c does not mean the conversion is incomplete. The driver commits from 2023-03-11 belong to a tree-wide series ('Replace all spi->chip_select and spi->cs_gpiod references with function call'), each a one-line mechanical swap to spi_get_chipselect(spi, 0). The 2023-12 follow-ups (tps6594, cs35l56) are the same kind of change. Commits that touch the SPI core after the API was added, such as be84be4a for SPI_INVALID_CS, can match on lines that already use the accessor plus moved comments, which gives false positives.
spi_get_chipselect.B: The old regex '->chip_select\b' over-matches. It also hits other structs (spi_board_info chip->chip_select, the ACPI lookup->chip_select, priv->spidev->chip_select through any pointer) and comments mentioning spi->chip_select[]. So raw remaining counts in spi.c overstate real spi_device leftovers. Most samples come from the March 2023 tree-wide series ('Replace all spi->chip_select and spi->cs_gpiod references with function call') or from late stragglers (Dec 2023), and they are clean one-line conversions to spi_get_chipselect(spi, 0). The new regex also matches lines where spi_set_chipselect/spi_get_chipselect calls already existed and only an argument changed (e.g. 0xFF -> SPI_INVALID_CS in be84be4a), which causes false positives in later spi core refactors.

strlcpy_strscpy.A: The old/new regexes (\bstrlcpy\s*\( and \bstrscpy\s*\() are precise for this migration. All 8 sampled commits are real API conversions, and most say so in the subject. Most commits are tree-wide Coccinelle or KSPP efforts (Joe Perches 2021, Wolfram Sang 2022, Azeem Shaikh and Kees Cook 2023) that convert only the strlcpy calls whose return value is unused. So partial conversions can show up wherever a return value is used, though none did in this sample. The bnxt commit (#2) is a refactor that converts only the calls it touches and leaves 4 others in the file, so the file-level completeness check matters. Where the return value is used (zfcp #7), the semantics change (strscpy returns -E2BIG instead of the source length), so those conversions need manual handling.
strlcpy_strscpy.B: The regexes are precise for this migration because strlcpy and strscpy have nearly identical call signatures, so most hits are 1:1 line swaps from KSPP's tree-wide strlcpy-removal campaign. Many of these commits are titled "Replace all non-returning strlcpy" and only convert calls whose return value is unused, so call sites that use the return value can stay behind. The return-value semantics differ: strlcpy returns the source length, while strscpy returns the copied length or -E2BIG. Where the return value is used (zfcp), the commit adds extra handling. Partial conversions also show up inside unrelated refactor commits that apply checkpatch fixes only to the touched functions (bnxt: 4 strlcpy left elsewhere in the file). In this sample no hits were coincidental.

strncpy_strscpy.B:
All 8 samples are deliberate strncpy cleanups; none is a coincidental regex hit. Common patterns:
- Converted code often drops a manual NUL-terminator line ("buf[sizeof(buf)-1] = '\0'") or a "- 1" in the length.
- Some strncpy calls are converted to memcpy instead of strscpy (qed). The "new" regex does not see those lines.
- Some go through a wrapper helper that calls strscpy, so the "new" regex matches only once, inside the helper (libfc fc_encode.h, a 2020 commit fixing a -Warray-bounds warning).
- strscpy_pad sometimes appears in its 2-argument form (uvesafb, 2024).
Two samples are partial because real strncpy calls remain in the same file: libfc has 2 left (fc_ct_ns_fill), zcrypt_api has 1 left (the nodename copy).
strncpy_strscpy.A: All 8 samples are deliberate strncpy() removals; most come from the KSPP/linux#90 strncpy-deprecation series (Justin Stitt, 2023-2024). A common pattern is `strncpy(...); buf[size-1] = '\0';` collapsing into a single strscpy() line. Some commits send part of the strncpy calls to memcpy (qed_debug) or to a new helper that wraps strscpy (libfc fc_encode.h, an older 2020 warning workaround). In that case the NEW regex only matches inside the helper definition, not at the converted call sites, so line-level pairing of old and new hits undercounts. Each commit usually fixes one call site, so other strncpy calls can remain in the same file (2 of 8 are partial). The old regex `\bstrncpy\s*\(` does not match strncpy_from_user(), so prefix false positives are not a concern. It can still hit comments or string literals, but none were seen here.

sysfs_emit.A: The old regex (sprintf/snprintf/scnprintf with a first argument of exactly 'buf') matches the main pattern in sysfs show() functions. It misses the append form 'scnprintf(buf + ret, PAGE_SIZE - ret, ...)', which is converted to sysfs_emit_at (sample #4). It can also match non-sysfs code that happens to name a local buffer 'buf', so a grep count on files that are not mostly sysfs code can overstate what is left. Most commits are coccinelle-driven cleanups (device_attr_show.cocci) and are often scoped to one function signature or one function family. That scoping leaves real leftovers, as in #0 (only device_attribute show functions converted, port_attribute ones not) and #1 (one function missed). In #5 the conversion happens because the line was rewritten for an error-handling fix, so file-level completeness should not be expected for that kind of commit.
sysfs_emit.B: The old regex only matches calls whose first argument is exactly 'buf', so it misses 'scnprintf(buf + ret, PAGE_SIZE - ret, ...)', which is converted to sysfs_emit_at (as in thunderbolt #4). It is also not limited to sysfs show callbacks, so in other files it can hit unrelated sprintf(buf, ...) calls on local buffers. The remaining matches in #0, #1 and #5 are all real sysfs show callbacks, so those are incomplete conversions. Many of these commits are tree-wide cocci series (Joe Perches) or one-file janitorial patches, and cocci scripts that only match the 'return ...' form tend to leave 'ret = snprintf(...)' forms behind (#1). Sample #5 shows a bug-fix commit that converts one line in passing, so a new sysfs_emit line next to a removed sprintf line does not always mean the commit is a migration.

tasklet_setup.A: All 8 samples come from the Kees Cook / Allen Pais tree-wide tasklet conversion series (late 2020 to early 2021). Each one replaces tasklet_init(t, fn, (unsigned long)data) with tasklet_setup(t, fn) and changes the callback from (unsigned long data) to (struct tasklet_struct *t) with from_tasklet(). The single-line old and new regexes are reliable for this pattern, and none of the files has tasklet_init left after its commit. One related change the regexes miss: direct assignments to tasklet.func become tasklet.callback (seen in i915).
tasklet_setup.B: All 8 samples are genuine and complete. Each one swaps tasklet_init(t, fn, (unsigned long)data) for tasklet_setup(t, fn), changes the callback signature from (unsigned long) to (struct tasklet_struct *t), and gets the context back with from_tasklet(). These are dedicated "use new tasklet API" commits from the 2020-2021 tree-wide conversion (Allen Pais / Kees Cook series), so the regex hits are not coincidental. The old regex \btasklet_init\s*\( is precise. It does not catch two related old-API usages: direct assignments to tasklet.func (i915 also converts these to .callback) and DECLARE_TASKLET with a data argument. So a file can show 0 tasklet_init matches and still have old-style tasklet usage in those forms.

timer_delete.B: The old regex '\bdel_timer(?:_sync)?\s*\(' covers both del_timer and del_timer_sync, so commits that convert only one variant (as in wireguard #0) show leftover hits of the other variant. Commits that are bug fixes (#1, #2) touch these lines as a side effect. Check whether sync semantics are preserved: del_timer_sync->timer_delete (non-sync), as in #2, is a semantic change, not a rename. timer_shutdown_sync additions can also appear alongside, and are a different API.
timer_delete.A: The old regex \bdel_timer(?:_sync)?\s*\( matches both del_timer and del_timer_sync, and the new regex matches both timer_delete and timer_delete_sync. So a commit that converts only one variant (like the wireguard commit, which converted only _sync) shows up as partial when the other variant is still in the file. Watch for cross-variant pairs, such as del_timer_sync -> timer_delete (non-sync) in dm-delay: both regexes hit, but the change in meaning is the real point and it is not a rename. Bug-fix commits (CVE fixes, race fixes) sometimes use the new names in passing, so read the commit message. Also note that timer_shutdown_sync (added in dm-delay) is a different API, and neither regex matches it. Kernel 6.15 later renamed del_timer* tree-wide, so later samples may come from large mechanical commits.

vm_flags_set.A: Only one sample, from the tree-wide commit 1c71222e5f23 by Suren Baghdasaryan ("mm: replace vma->vm_flags direct modifications with modifier calls"). It changes many files, and each file's hunks are mechanical conversions: |= becomes vm_flags_set, &= ~ becomes vm_flags_clear. Because the old regex starts with '->', git grep needs '-e' in front of the pattern; without it, git reads the pattern as an option and exits with code 129. The old regex also misses plain assignments ('vma->vm_flags = ...', which became vm_flags_init/vm_flags_reset), and the new regex has no entry for vm_flags_reset.
vm_flags_set.B: The old regex starts with '->', so git grep reads it as an option unless it is passed with -e. The command template in the task fails with exit 129 ('unknown switch >'), which could be mistaken for 'no matches'. Use 'git grep -c -P -e <regex>'. The old regex matches only compound assignment (|=, &=). It misses plain assignments such as 'vma->vm_flags = ...', which vm_flags_init/vm_flags_reset would replace. Sample #0 comes from the tree-wide commit 1c71222e5f23 ('mm: replace vma->vm_flags direct modifications with modifier calls'), which touches many files. Other files from that commit should be genuine too, but check each one for leftover usages.
